notes: The ONE industry vocabulary for the Digital Room, plus the rules for mapping a messy CRM value onto it. Read by app/src/industries.ts, by tools/build-catalog.mjs when tagging assets, and by the Cognigy lookup_crm tool, so the portal and the live agent can never disagree about which vertical a visitor is in.
why: Salesforce Industry is not a picklist in practice: across a large account base the field holds well over a thousand distinct values. The same vertical appears as 'Financial Services', 'Finance and Insurance', 'Banks', 'Banking', 'Finance' and 'Banks & Credit Cards'; healthcare appears four ways. Several values also carry an invisible zero-width character, so 'Healthcare' and 'Healthcare\u200b' are different strings to a computer and identical to a human. Matching raw values would silently miss a large share of accounts, so everything is normalised at the boundary instead.
canonical: The twelve industries NiCE itself filters by on nice.com/resources. Authoritative, already carried by the 27 curated documents, and the slug deep-links to NiCE's own filtered listing: https://www.nice.com/resources?industries=<slug>
deliberatelyPartial: Big Salesforce industries with no NiCE vertical (Manufacturing, Computer Services/Consulting beyond Technology, Professional Services, Construction/Real Estate, Transportation and Warehousing) are NOT forced into the nearest-looking box. They return null, which makes the room ask the visitor instead. A wrong vertical is worse than no vertical: it puts the wrong customer story in front of them.

exactOverrides._why: Values whose keywords point two ways at once, or whose wording matches nothing useful. Applied BEFORE the alias rules, so they win. 'Finance and Insurance' is the important one: it is a census-style bucket containing both, and alias order alone would send every bank in it to Insurance.

junk._why: Values that exist but say nothing. A large share of accounts sit here. Treated as no answer, which is what makes the fallback question a normal path rather than an edge case.
